title: Meadow vs Dutchie: 2026 Dispensary POS Comparison
summary: Meadow vs Dutchie compared for 2026: e-commerce, delivery, 4/20 reliability, pricing, payments, and support, plus which dispensaries each platform fits.
body_markdown:

**This guide compares Meadow and Dutchie on reliability, delivery, pricing, online ordering, support, and state coverage, then shows who each platform fits. If you're on Dutchie now, it also covers what switching involves.**

## Key Takeaways


- Meadow has had 100% uptime on every 4/20 since 2015, while Dutchie had documented 4/20 outages in 2023 and 2024.
- Meadow runs hub-and-spoke, dynamic (ice cream truck), and hybrid delivery natively in the POS, and was the first cannabis software company to launch dynamic delivery in California.
- Meadow charges one flat monthly fee per location with unlimited seats, flexible contracts, no per-transaction fees, and your choice of payment processor, while Dutchie's free hardware requires Dutchie Pay.
- Meadow menus run on your own site, synced to register inventory and connected to Weedmaps and Leafly, so every online order and customer record stays with your store.

## What to Look for in Dispensary Software


The right dispensary POS stays up on your busiest day, runs every sales channel from one inventory, and costs what you expected once payments and add-ons are counted. Your[dispensary POS system](https://getmeadow.com/features/point-of-sale) runs[inventory management](https://getmeadow.com/features/inventory-management) , keeps you in line with[state compliance](https://getmeadow.com/features/metrc-compliance) , and powers the[online menus](https://getmeadow.com/features/ecommerce) ,[loyalty programs](https://getmeadow.com/features/loyalty-and-rewards) , and[delivery](https://getmeadow.com/features/cannabis-delivery) your customers expect, so a weak link anywhere costs you sales or creates compliance risk.


When comparing Meadow and Dutchie, focus on the four areas where they differ most:


- **Reliability:** How has the system performed on 4/20 and other peak days?
- **Delivery and Online Ordering:** Which delivery models come standard, and who owns the online storefront?
- **Total Cost:** What do you pay across POS, payments, and add-ons, and can you choose your payment processor?
- **Support and Coverage:** How fast does a real person respond, and does the platform support every state you operate in?

## Dutchie Overview


Dutchie is a cannabis POS and e-commerce platform that began with online menus and consumer ordering, then added point of sale and its own payment processing, Dutchie Pay.


**Dutchie's Core Features:**


- **POS:** Dual-screen terminals and inventory tracking.
- **Compliance Tools:** ID verification and purchase limits.
- **Online Ordering:** Menus plus listings in Dutchie's consumer marketplace.
- **Delivery:** Standard (pizza-style) delivery in the POS, with dynamic delivery as an add-on and route optimization through an Onfleet integration.


**Consider Dutchie if:** You operate in a BioTrack state.


**Dutchie Watch-Outs:**


- **Peak-Day Reliability:** Documented 4/20 outages in 2023 and 2024.
- **Payment Lock-In:** Free hardware requires Dutchie Pay, which limits your flexibility on processing costs.
- **Platform Changes:** As of the writing of this article, Dutchie has said it will support legacy Dutchie Plus storefronts only through the end of 2026.[Learn what the Dutchie Plus sunset means for your store.](https://getmeadow.com/blog/dutchie-plus-sunset)

## Comparing Meadow and Dutchie


Meadow and Dutchie differ most on peak-day reliability, delivery track record, pricing structure, and who owns the online storefront.


### Reliability


Meadow has had 100% uptime on every 4/20 since 2015, and Dutchie had documented outages on 4/20, the busiest sales day of the year, in both 2023 and 2024.


- **Meadow:** 99.999% uptime since 2014, and 100% uptime on every 4/20 since 2015.
- **Dutchie:** Outages on 4/20 in 2023 and 2024, per MJBizDaily reporting. As of the writing of this article, these are the most recent documented 4/20 outages.


For more on Dutchie's track record, see[Jane vs Dutchie: 2026 Dispensary POS Comparison](https://getmeadow.com/blog/jane-vs-dutchie) .


### Delivery Management


Meadow runs hub-and-spoke, dynamic, and hybrid delivery natively in the POS, and it was the first cannabis software company to launch dynamic delivery in California.


- **Meadow:** All three models, including dynamic ([Ice Cream Truck](https://getmeadow.com/blog/how-to-launch-mobile-dispensary-ice-cream-truck-delivery) ) delivery, with geofencing, built-in dispatch, and California delivery ledger compliance. Onfleet is optional for live GPS tracking and route optimization. Meadow[launched Dynamic Delivery in California in 2021](https://techcrunch.com/2021/11/16/meadow-launches-dynamic-delivery-to-bring-mobile-cannabis-dispensaries-to-california/) , bringing mobile, on-demand dispensary delivery to the state.
- **Dutchie:** Standard, pizza-style delivery is part of Dutchie POS, with dynamic delivery available as an add-on. Route optimization and real-time driver tracking run through its Onfleet integration.


See how[Meadow's delivery platform](https://getmeadow.com/features/cannabis-delivery) handles all three models. Planning to launch or expand delivery? ### Pricing and Payments


Meadow charges one flat monthly fee per location with unlimited seats, flexible contracts, and no per-transaction fees; Dutchie quotes custom contracts and ties its free hardware to Dutchie Pay.

For more on how POS pricing works, see[Cannabis POS Pricing: What Dispensaries Actually Pay in 2026](https://getmeadow.com/blog/cannabis-pos-pricing) .

Your customer and order data belongs to your store: Meadow never sells it or uses it to help your competitors.
- **Dutchie:** Online menus plus listings in Dutchie's consumer marketplace, where shoppers browse your store next to nearby competitors.

## The High Cost of a Fragmented Stack


When one platform doesn't cover a job end to end, operators fill the gaps with add-on subscriptions and third-party tools: a delivery add-on here, a payment processor there. That approach can lead to:


- **Increased Costs:** Separate subscriptions, transaction charges, and costs that don't show up on the first quote.
- **Operational Inefficiencies:** Systems that don't integrate well lead to delays, errors, and double entry.
- **Staff Training Challenges:** Employees must learn multiple products.
- **Compromised Customer Experience:** Poorly connected systems slow down service.


To compare platforms fairly, add up the real number: POS, e-commerce, payments, and any delivery add-on, multiplied by your locations.

## Put Your Current Setup to the Test


The fastest way to see what your current POS costs you is to run four everyday tasks on it, then run the same tasks in a Meadow demo.


1. **Add a flash sale to your online menu.** Count the screens and systems it takes, and check whether the price updates at the register too.
2. **Train a new budtender.** If it takes more than a shift before they can ring a sale alone, turnover is costing you sales.
3. **Run a delivery.** Check whether dispatch, routing, and compliance live in the same system as your sales.
4. **Get help when something breaks.** Time how long it takes a real person to respond.


If two or more feel painful, your current setup is costing you time. For a step-by-step migration plan, see[How to Switch Dispensary POS Without Losing a Day of Sales](https://getmeadow.com/blog/dispensary-pos-migration) .

## Final Thoughts: Meadow vs Dutchie


Meadow is the stronger fit for dispensaries in its six states that run delivery, can't afford downtime on peak days, and want one platform on one flat fee. Dutchie fits a narrower case.


**Consider Dutchie if** you run stores in BioTrack states. The trade-offs are documented 4/20 outages in 2023 and 2024 and free hardware that requires Dutchie Pay.


**Choose Meadow if:**


- Delivery is core to your business, or will be
- Reliability on peak days is non-negotiable
- You want one platform, one bill, and one support team
- You want to own your storefront and choose your payment processor

## Meadow vs Dutchie FAQs


### Is Meadow or Dutchie better for dispensaries?


Meadow is the better fit for dispensaries in California, New York, New Jersey, Massachusetts, Michigan, and Minnesota that run delivery, need uptime on peak days, and want one platform on one flat fee. Dutchie fits operators with stores in BioTrack states. For more options, see[Best Dutchie Alternatives in 2026](https://getmeadow.com/blog/dutchie-alternatives) .


### Has Dutchie gone down on 4/20?


Dutchie had documented outages on 4/20 in both 2023 and 2024, per MJBizDaily. Meadow has had 100% uptime on every 4/20 since 2015.


### Can I switch from Dutchie to Meadow?


Yes. Meadow's onboarding team handles data migration, Metrc cleanup, inventory imports, and staff training, and dispensaries like[West Coast Collective](https://getmeadow.com/blog/how-xzibits-west-coast-collective-made-the-switch-to-meadow-without-missing) have switched with zero downtime. Check your Dutchie contract and renewal date first, then follow the steps in[How to Switch Dispensary POS Without Losing a Day of Sales](https://getmeadow.com/blog/dispensary-pos-migration) .


### Will I lose my Dutchie e-commerce traffic if I switch?


You keep your direct traffic and your Weedmaps and Leafly listings, and your menu runs on your own site, synced to register inventory. Orders that come through Dutchie's consumer marketplace won't follow you, so measure how much revenue arrives through it before you set a switch date.


### How much do Meadow and Dutchie cost?


Meadow charges one flat monthly fee per location with unlimited seats, flexible contracts, and no per-transaction fees, quoted in your demo for the plan and locations you need. Dutchie quotes custom contracts rather than publishing pricing, and its free hardware requires Dutchie Pay.


### What is happening with Dutchie Plus?


As of the writing of this article, Dutchie has said it will support legacy Dutchie Plus storefronts only through the end of 2026. Dispensaries running custom storefronts on Plus need to move them before support ends. See our guide to[what dispensaries should do next](https://getmeadow.com/blog/dutchie-plus-sunset) .
